seoTitle: Copy Columns to Another Sheet in Smartsheet
metaDescription: Transfer column structures and data between Smartsheet sheets using Copy Row to Another Sheet or the Save as New protocol for cloning templates.
intro: Rebuilding the same column setup from scratch every time you start a new sheet is a waste of effort. Smartsheet gives you a couple of ways to replicate columns, whether you want to move live data across or just clone the structure as a template. This guide covers both approaches.

steps.heading: Select your source columns or rows
steps.body: Open your primary sheet and select the specific columns or row blocks you want to replicate.

steps.heading: Use Copy Row to Another Sheet
steps.body: Push your structural column data into a secondary destination file using this native tool.

steps.heading: Preserve validation settings
steps.body: Check that custom column validation, multi-select picklists, and contact assignments carry over correctly.

steps.heading: Or clone with Save as New
steps.body: Use the Save as New protocol to duplicate a clean grid structure as a reusable template without live data.

steps.heading: Verify header mapping
steps.body: Map headers carefully to avoid mismatched data entries or broken layout dependencies in the destination sheet.

faq.question: Can I copy just the column structure without the data?
faq.answer: Yes, the Save as New protocol lets you clone a grid structure as a reusable template without carrying over live data.

faq.question: Will dropdown settings transfer when I copy columns?
faq.answer: Custom column validation and multi-select picklists are designed to carry over, but it's worth verifying after the copy.

faq.question: What's the risk of mismatched headers?
faq.answer: Mismatched headers can cause data entries to land in the wrong fields or break layout dependencies, so mapping them carefully matters.

faq.question: Does copying preserve parent-child row hierarchies?
faq.answer: Preserving hierarchies during ingestion is something to check, since configuration limits and formatting shifts can occur.
